summary:
Signals from Mars is a bilingual interactive educational website that brings the stories of eight NASA robots on Mars to life through fictional radio transmissions inspired by real missions.

Designed for students aged 9–13, the experience invites visitors to operate a virtual radio receiver, locate spacecraft on an interactive 3D globe of Mars, and discover their stories through first-person narration, authentic NASA photographs, 3D models, and educational mini-games.

Each robot shares its arrival, engineering design, scientific discoveries, and final days. Activities help users understand how these machines worked and how unexpected challenges sometimes led to important breakthroughs, such as Spirit's damaged wheel revealing silica-rich soil.

By combining storytelling, scientific accuracy, and interactive exploration, Signals from Mars transforms silent robotic explorers into memorable characters and demonstrates how past missions continue to shape the future of space exploration.
details:
Project Overview

Signals from Mars is an interactive storytelling experience designed to introduce children aged 9–13 to the history of NASA's robotic exploration of Mars.

Instead of presenting a conventional encyclopedia of space missions, our project transforms the visitor into the operator of a fictional radio receiver. By tuning into eight silent spacecraft — Viking 1, Viking 2, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, and Ingenuity — users discover their stories through first-person narratives grounded in official NASA mission records.

How It Works

Visitors select a spacecraft using a radio tuning dial, an interactive 3D globe of Mars, or a flat map showing real mission coordinates.

Each spacecraft has four narrative chapters: Arrival, My Body, What I Discovered, and My Last Day. The experience combines narrated stories, authentic NASA photographs, interactive 3D models, and educational mini-activities.

Every mini-game explores a scientific or engineering concept. For example, users can simulate how Spirit's damaged wheel uncovered silica-rich soil, drive Sojourner toward Martian rocks, explore InSight's seismic investigations, or follow Ingenuity's historic flights.

Visitors can also compare mission lifetimes, explore connections between generations of spacecraft, collect mission cards, and unlock a personalized Mars Guardian certificate.

Educational Impact and Creativity

Our goal is to make planetary science engaging, accessible, and emotionally meaningful.

The project emphasizes the relationship between engineering and scientific discovery, demonstrating how robotic explorers continued contributing to humanity's knowledge even when their missions encountered unexpected problems.

Its main creative element is the fictional radio-receiver experience, which allows silent machines to tell their own stories while maintaining a clear distinction between historical facts and imaginative narration.

Technology and Accessibility

The application was developed as a single HTML file using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript. It integrates Three.js for interactive 3D visualization, the Web Speech API for narration, the Web Audio API for sound effects, and localStorage for saving progress.

Scientific information comes from NASA's NSSDCA and NASA Science resources, supported by official mission imagery, 3D assets, and audio recordings.

The website supports Spanish and English, responsive layouts, light and dark themes, and reduced-motion accessibility preferences.
